ir.title: Infrared Spectroscopy (IR) — Vibrational frequencies (cm⁻¹)
ir.principle: IR measures molecular vibrations. Frequency ν ∝ √(k/μ) (Hooke's law: stronger bond ↑ν, heavier atom ↓ν). Region 4000-400 cm⁻¹. Fingerprint region 1500-400 cm⁻¹ is unique per molecule. Strong bands require change in dipole moment.

tables.notes: Sharp free alcohol/phenol; in dilute solution
Broad due to H-bonding network; increases as conc. increases
Extremely broad overlapping C-H; characteristic very wide band due to dimer H-bonding
1° amine: 2 peaks (asym/sym); 2°: 1 peak; 3°: none; amide similar but ~3350
Internal alkyne weak; terminal medium; symmetric dialkyl alkyne may be IR-inactive
Amide I band ~1650; amide II ~1550 (N-H bend)
Weak if symmetric trans; conjugation lowers to ~1620
Two bands ~1600 & ~1500 due to ring; overtone/combination 2000-1650 pattern indicates substitution
1050 primary, ~1100 secondary, ~1150 tertiary; phenol ~1200; ester 2 bands 1300-1000

interpretationTips: Check 4000-2500 first: broad 3300-2500 + 1710 → carboxylic acid; broad 3400-3200 → alcohol (exchangeable); sharp 3300 → alkyne; twin 2720/2820 + 1720 → aldehyde
Strong 1700±50 → carbonyl: use exact ν + O-H to classify acid vs ester vs ketone vs aldehyde vs amide.
Absence of strong carbonyl but 1650 + 3080 → alkene; 1600+1500+3030 → aromatic.
Fingerprint 1500-400 distinguishes isomers; match to library.

nmr.title: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR)
nmr.principle: NMR measures magnetic environment of nuclei (¹H, ¹³C) in applied field. Chemical shift δ (ppm) referenced to TMS (0 ppm). Shielding ↑ → δ ↓. Integration ∝ number of H; multiplicity (n+1 rule) from vicinal H count (J coupling constant ~7 Hz for alkyl, 2 Hz for geminal, 10 cis/17 trans for vinyl). Exchangeable OH/NH are broad singlets.

hNmrShifts.type: CH α to heteroatom (C-O, C-N, C-X)
hNmrShifts.notes: Electronegative atom deshields; CH3-OAc ~2.0 for acetyl
Conjugated or substituted shifts more downfield

hNmrShifts.example: Ph-H 7.27; electron-donor OMe shields (6.8), NO2 deshields (8.2)
hNmrShifts.notes: Ring current strongly deshields; substitution pattern from splitting
Exchangeable; often very broad, disappears with D2O
Variable; exchangeable with D2O, no splitting; may not appear
Exchangeable; may be broad due to quadrupole

nmr.splittingRules: n equivalent vicinal H on adjacent carbon → n+1 peaks (doublet =1 neighbor, triplet=2, quartet=3, quintet=4). Coupling constant J (Hz) reveals connectivity: vicinal (³J) ~7 (alkyl), 6-12 cis / 14-18 trans (vinyl), 1-10 allylic; geminal (²J) ~2. Ethyl pattern: CH3 triplet (n=2) integrates 3H + CH2 quartet (n=3) integrates 2H with same J (~7 Hz).
nmr.deuterium: Shaking with D2O exchanges OH/NH/SH → signal disappears, confirms exchangeable proton.

massSpec.title: Mass Spectrometry (MS)
massSpec.principle: Molecule ionized (EI, 70 eV) → molecular ion M⁺· (m/z = molecular weight). Fragments by homolysis/heterolysis. Base peak = most intense (100%). Isotope pattern: ³⁵Cl/³⁷Cl 3:1, ⁷⁹Br/⁸¹Br 1:1, M+2 reveals halogen count. Nitrogen rule: odd M = odd N (for M⁺).

commonFragmentations.description: Bond breaks α to O/N: R-CH2-CH2-O· → R-CH2· + CH2=O⁺ (e.g., alcohol gives CH2=OH⁺ m/z 31)
Carbonyl with γ-H → 6-membered TS, transfers H to carbonyl O, cleaves α-β, forms enol radical cation. E.g., hexanal CH3CH2CH2CH2CHO → m/z 44 (CH2=CHOH⁺·)
Alkylbenzene cleaves benzylic bond → stable tropylium C7H7⁺ m/z 91 base peak (rearranges to aromatic 7-membered).
Alkene cleaves allylic → resonance-stabilized allyl cation.
Common neutrals lost: H2O (M-18, alcohol), CH3· (M-15), Et· (M-29), CO (M-28, carbonyl/phenol), CO2 (M-44, acid/ester).
Deduce formula: Cl: M:M+2 3:1; 2Cl 9:6:1; Br 1:1; 2Br 1:2:1; S gives M+2 4% per S.
commonFragmentations.tip: Odd m/z molecular ion → odd N

interpretationSteps: 1. Find M⁺· (highest m/z, may be weak for alcohols/branched). Check nitrogen rule and isotope pattern for Cl/Br.
2. Base peak (100%) often is most stable carbocation (tertiary, allylic, benzylic, α-cleavage).
3. Look for M-18 (alcohol), M-31 (OCH3), M-43 (CH3CO), M-91 (benzyl).
4. Fragment mass differences reveal neutral losses; combine with IR/NMR to assign structure.

combinedProblemExample.unknown: C4H8O: IR 1715 strong, no broad O-H, ¹H NMR: δ 2.1 (s,3H), 2.4 (t,2H), 0.9 (t,3H); MS M⁺ 72 base 43
combinedProblemExample.solution: IR C=O ketone; NMR singlet 3H = CH3CO; triplet 2H + triplet 3H = ethyl CH2CH3; structure CH3COCH2CH3 (butan-2-one). MS 43 = CH3CO⁺, M 72 correct.
